title: Valkyries Win WNBA Title in Only Their Second Season
summary:
The Golden State Valkyries defeated the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in a thrilling Game 7 on October 31, 2026, to capture their first WNBA championship. They also made history by becoming the first WNBA expansion team to win a title in just their second season.

An expansion team is a brand new sports team added to an existing league. It is usually created to bring a team to a city or area that did not previously have one. The San Francisco-based Valkyries joined the WNBA as its 13th team in 2025. In their first season, they won 23 games, more than any other expansion team, and became the first expansion team to reach the playoffs in their inaugural season.

The second year was just as impressive. The team finished the regular season with 32 wins and 12 losses, earning the second seed in the playoffs. They then defeated the Dallas Wings in the first round and the defending champion Las Vegas Aces in the semifinals. The final against the Atlanta Dream turned into a close battle. After six games, the series was tied at three wins apiece, setting up the first deciding Game 7 in WNBA Finals history.

Trailing by six points at halftime in front of their home crowd at Chase Center, the Valkyries mounted a second-half comeback. Gabby Williams led the effort, scoring 28 points to set a WNBA postseason record for the most points in a half. She also made a key three-pointer late in the game, helping Golden State secure the victory. Her outstanding performance earned her the WNBA Finals Most Valuable Player, or MVP, award.
why_it_matters: A brand new team winning so fast shows that a young team can reach the top quickly, and it gives Bay Area fans a new championship team to cheer.
